title: Featured performers and organist Ray McNamara
summary: DeDroit mentions Edna Orman and John Hammond, earning extra for solos, and organist Ray McNamara.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: And it was so great. We had Edna Orman and we had, oh, John Hammond, he came down here from New York, he was featured and he had big money at the same. They could play. I used to make a lot of extra money playing with him. I'd play solos. He wouldn't know what to do and they used to put him on for a feature number. So every once in a while he'd cash in on the fact that everybody liked me, or I think so anyhow, and I'd make a few bucks extra by playing a solo. Like East I might play the Hover City or something like that. And every week I had a program with Ray McNamara who incidentally was a very fine organist. You heard of Ray McNamara? You have, haven't you?
The name's familiar. He was at WWL.
He played dance music too. Ray was a composer. I think he's a member of VASCAP. He gets a check. Well you recorded one of his tunes. What? Well, I was getting back to the guitar and the banjo.
